onlyInCSR: Every loan you have, on one screen.

Four years of school usually means eight separate federal loans, and nowhere that shows them together. Add yours once to see what you owe, which repayment plans you can actually use, and what extra money would change.
For each loan: what you owe, the interest rate, and the date it was paid out. All three are at studentaid.gov under My Aid.
Not near your login? Start with the example loans and swap in your own numbers later.
All of it. There is no account and no server. What you type is saved in this browser and goes nowhere else.
Nothing here is for sale, and nothing is trying to refinance you.

Everything you type stays in this browser. There is no account, no server, and no analytics. Nothing you enter is transmitted anywhere, and closing the tab does not send it either. The math here is ordinary arithmetic run on your device, not an AI model.

These are estimates, not financial advice. The right plan depends on things this tool does not know, like whether your income is about to change or what else you owe. Your servicer sets your actual payment, and studentaid.gov is the authority on your account.
Built by Cense, a free weekly personal finance newsletter for people who did not get taught this.
